messages:
miriam: Quick idea — low-cost optimization: do a tiny span-coalescing pass at ingest to collapse lots of sub-100ms helper spans (mobile heartbeats, short library RPCs). Thought itd be good to discuss tradeoffs before I prototype.

devon: Curious how you identify candidates — name-based? timing? parent/trace matching?

miriam: Plan: candidate if same trace_id+parent_id+effective_route, name in configurable whitelist, and start times within a sliding window (150	60ms). Emit one synthetic span with merged_count, raw_sum_cost, merge_bucket, merge_window_ms.

anish: Danger: retry storms or hedged requests may be masked, losing visibility into failure patterns. Also percentiles will shift since we're removing individual samples.

sam: And watch grpc/streaming flows where multiple short spans are semantically separate.

miriam: Safety rules: no merge if span.error=true, streaming=true, duration>1s, explicit dont_merge flag, or differing caller identity/downstream endpoint. Also whitelist-only by default.

katie: For billing: do we sum tokens/bytes for the synthetic span or compute a smoothed/ capped value? If we just sum it could spike a customer's bill in a minute.

miriam: We keep raw_sum_cost for audit and compute smoothed_cost for dashboards/billing UI. Heuristic: smoothed = min(raw_sum, baseline + alpha * sqrt(raw_sum)). Baseline is per-tenant+route and only created when traffic > threshold (1rps over 60s) to avoid per-tenant state explosion. Global fallback baseline if missing.

devon: Baseline TTL and decay matter — must shrink baseline when traffic drops to avoid stale caps. Also track baseline generation metadata for debugging.

sam: How does this play with sampling? If traces are sampled downstream, merged_count/raw_sum need to be preserved and upsampled by the sampling factor.

miriam: We'll run merge before sampling. The sampled payload will include merged_count and raw_sum; billing pipeline multiplies raw_sum by sampling_inverse if present and marks estimates when not.

anish: Suggest adding merge_bucket/version and merge_reason fields so dashboards can filter and so we can roll out different heuristics. Also add merge_id referencing original span ids (bounded list) for deep-dive.

miriam: Good call. Example emitted metadata: merged:true, merged_count:5, merge_bucket:"coalesce-short-v1", merge_reason:"idempotent-helper", merge_window_ms:300, raw_sum_cost:210, smoothed_cost:140, merge_refs:["a1","a2","a3"]. Well cap merge_refs length to avoid bloat.

katie: Need to ensure billing pipeline accepts raw_sum + sampling factor and an estimate flag. Also product wants to know when we applied smoothing vs raw for chargeback.

devon: Ops plan: canary in prod region for 2 weeks. Metrics to collect: ingest CPU, storage change, query fidelity (compare top-100 flows percentile deltas), and billing diff. Also track false-positive merges.

miriam: Action items:
- miriam: prototype ingest coalescer at gateway with whitelist + safety rules + merge metadata.
- devon: design baseline service (per-route/tenant) with TTL/decay and threshold logic.
- katie: validate billing pipeline and add estimate flag handling.
- anish: create comparison dashboards for percentiles/counts pre/post.
- sam: identify candidate non-sensitive routes/customers for canary.

ops-bot: created ticket INF-8201 span coalescing prototype (epic: obs-cost-optim).

sam: Please add a feature-flag and route/customer toggle so we can roll selectively.

miriam: Will add flags and a short RFC tomorrow with sample queries and a few example datasets. Thanks all :thumbsup:
